areas.why: Presumed ISA 240 revenue fraud risk is live here: the sale price is a multiple of FY2025 EBITDA and the buyer wants accounts fast (N2), and a 156,250 net (187,500 gross) Brightwater 'final account' was booked as a manual journal on 11 Feb 2026, backdated to 30 Dec 2025, unapproved, posted at 19:42 by the person who raises every invoice, reusing invoice number INV-2025-1499 that was already issued to Wetherby Care Homes in June. It is the only FY25 debtor not received by 23 Feb 2026, and Martin only said it was 'agreed in principle' (N5). Revenue is recognised on payment-schedule invoices, not stage of completion, for three contracts spanning the year end (N5), and last year's cut-off misstatement was 22,000 (FY24-08).

Trade debtors went from 158,427 to 670,815. Of the 103 open FY25 invoices, 102 were settled in full in the Q1 2026 bank statement. The one that was not is MJ-000024 Brightwater 187,500, which is 3.75x overall materiality and has no third-party evidence. Retentions of 5% (N5) do not appear anywhere: there is no retention debtor, and housing invoices were paid in full.

A new subcontractor shows the classic signs of a fictitious supplier. Wharfedale Site Services (S033) started in July with no contract, introduced by a site foreman (N11). It sent 9 invoices of 9,594 to 9,979 gross, all just under the 10,000 MD-approval limit, all posted AND approved by tom.finance (the only purchase invoices he posted apart from the refurbishment), with non-sequential references (WSS-887, -627, -548, -282, -239...). They were paid in about 7 days against a 27-day norm, 87,172 gross in total, and it explains half the 35% rise in subcontractor costs against 18% revenue growth. The approval control was also bypassed by splitting MTH-77120 into two 7,400 parts (PI-000773/774), paid as a single 14,800 BACS line (B25-00856). The FY24 duplicate-payment finding repeated at the same supplier: PCS-88231 and PCS88231 were both paid (B25-00628, B25-00646), despite management saying it was fixed (N19).

Callum Reed (E019) left on 30 Jun 2025 but was paid 2,331 net every month from July to December (B25-01153, B25-01350, B25-01566, B25-01749, B25-01959, B25-02152), 13,986 net in total. That repeats FY24-14, which management said was addressed (N19), and contradicts 'one or two' leavers and 'flat at 24' (N6). Payroll is identical every month (74,500 gross, 5,513,000p net) with no starters or leavers reflected. Tom runs the payroll, approves the PR journals and prepares the BACS (N3, N6). There are no pension contributions anywhere in the ledger or bank despite auto-enrolment and a scheme move in September (N7). Tom's start date is 2024-05-01 in parties.csv and Feb 2025 in N3, and he was paid in Jan 2025. Amounts are below PM, so elevated rather than significant, but the partner may lift it given the repeat and the fraud indicators.

Risk is low despite the size (memo item 4): last year 30 hours on the register found nothing (FY24-01, FY24-16). The only addition above PM is the Transit Custom at 61,250 (PI-000754, N4). Points to cover inside standard FA-01: a van service/MOT/tyres invoice of 1,840 capitalised to 0050 (PI-000775); the split Moorland kit invoice (PI-000773/774); depreciation is a flat 6,500 a month all year with no charge for the ~102k of additions.

I matched every statement line to the ledger. The ledger bank balance (1,031,635.09) is 9,500 below the statement (1,041,135.09, B25-02197). The whole difference is MJ-000019, a 'Transfer' journal the MD posted at 20:05 on 21 Nov, crediting bank and debiting advertising, with no matching bank line, no support and no approval. Other manual journals to bank: MJ-000016 and MJ-000020.

MJ-000016 is a 35,000 advance to Martin Ashworth, posted by Martin himself at 19:12 and unapproved (B25-00843). It sits in other debtors at the year end and was not repaid by 23 Feb 2026. That breaches the s.197 10,000 threshold again, repeating FY24-03 after management said it was addressed (N19). The company also paid 24,000 + VAT to Ashworth Property Ltd (S029, Martin's company) to refurbish Ashworth Property's own unit. It was expensed as rent, with no board minute (N8), and paid in 1 day (B25-02094). MISC-OPS includes a 1,200 'Gift - chairman's 60th' (PI-000771). Helen Ashworth (E002, related) controls HR (N6). The pending sale (N2) raises the stakes on disclosure.

Management has a strong incentive (EBITDA-based sale price, N2), and both the MD and the FM post manual journals with no approver (N3, N16). Of the 24 manual journals, 4 are unapproved entries by management, three of them after hours: MJ-000016 (advance to the MD), MJ-000019 (bank 'Transfer' with no bank line), MJ-000020 (2,500 staff loan to J Price coded to subcontractors 5100) and MJ-000024 (backdated 156k revenue reusing an invoice number). Also MJ-000017/018 accrues 12,000 and reverses 10,200. PI-000776 is unbalanced: a 624 VAT line is missing, so ledger 2201 does not agree to the TB.

Cash is over 1.0m at the year end and 1.29m by 23 Feb 2026, there are no borrowings (overdraft cancelled), there are no covenants, and profit before tax is 1.16m (N9, N1). The pending sale and a possible VAT exposure (see vat) are disclosure and subsequent-events points, not doubts over going concern.

There is no stock or WIP account in the chart or TB; materials (2.13m) are expensed as purchased. Unbilled work on the three contracts spanning the year end is dealt with under revenue (REV-04). I would confirm with the client that van/stores stock is immaterial.

This is our fourth year with an unmodified prior-year opinion (N18). Opening TB equals the prior-year closing and balances to zero, so OB-01 does not apply. Two specific opening items are picked up elsewhere: the 9,500 opening accrual was never reversed (accrualsProvisions), and closing retained earnings (480,573) look inconsistent with the 878,867 prior-year profit in the comparatives (a partner question).

The VAT returns posted in the ledger do not agree to the ledger's own VAT. The Q2 transfer (MJ-000010) declares output VAT of 18,005 against 238,148 in the ledger and claims a 30,553 repayment (B25-01230). The ledger implies about 68,800 was payable. Q4 2025 also produced an HMRC repayment of 3,013 (B26-00140) against ledger net VAT due of about 113,500. Inputs are also under-claimed in Q1 to Q3, so at the year end the control accounts carry 160,976 net owed (2200 -498,504, 2201 +337,528) while 2202 shows nil. About 47,500 of that relates to quarters already filed. That is roughly 1x materiality of under-declaration, with penalty and interest exposure and a possible deliberate-misstatement and money-laundering-reporting angle. The preparer, Jane, leaves in April (N15). Repeats from last year: client dinner coded to advertising with VAT reclaimed (PI-000770, repeats FY24-06); T1 lines with zero VAT at Calder Fixings (PI-000757..759, repeats FY24-13). Subcontractors all charge 20% VAT where the CIS domestic reverse charge may apply.

The only debit to accruals all year is MJ-000018. The 9,500 opening accrual was never reversed, repeating FY24-07 although management said accruals now carry a reversal flag (N19). The Wharfedale accrual of 12,000 was reversed at 10,200, leaving 1,800. Closing accruals of 41,650 include a new 14,200 holiday-pay estimate. Missing from the TB entirely: corporation tax on 1.16m profit (no tax accounts), pension accruals (N7) and the VAT exposure above.

There is substantial laws-and-regulations exposure: VAT returns misstated, no pension contributions under auto-enrolment (N7), possible s.197 breach, CIS status of new subcontractor Wharfedale (FY24-17 precedent), and no CIS liability account in the TB. A pending sale (N2) and possible fraud indicators need to go to those charged with governance and may need an MLRO consideration. Fee and timetable pressure from the MD (N2, N10) is a quality-management point.

hoursEstimateVsBudget: Inadequate. Selected procedures at the extents above come to roughly 155-165h. By area: revenue ~45 (REV-02 at 40 samples ~20-24h, REV-04 10), debtors ~13, purchases ~23, payroll ~14, FA ~4, bank ~9, RP ~11, journals ~18 (all 24 manual journals plus risk sample), GC 3, VAT ~8, accruals ~4, completion ~6. The 120h budget holds only if significant areas are cut, which is exactly what the memo forbids. Savings already taken: FA held at baseline, which frees ~27h against last year's 30h actual, and BNK-03, PAY-03 and REV-05 are largely pre-computed from the ledger and bank files. I would report a 35-45h overrun to Ingrid and ask for a budget increase rather than trim REV-02/REV-04, VAT-01 or PUR-03.
